chunks: In truth they are in doubt that they will ever face their Lord. Do they not know that He surrounds all things?
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'miryah' (doubt) in the context of meeting the Lord?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to refute the materialist denial of the Hereafter, emphasizing that while disbelievers harbor doubt about meeting their Lord, God’s omnipresence and omniscience encompass every hidden and apparent reality. It underscores the theological principle that divine knowledge is not limited by human perception, reinforcing the certainty of resurrection as a logical consequence of God’s all-encompassing nature.
